text:
elaine: Heads-up — found partner webhook logs in S3 that include tenant-scoped service tokens. :rotating_light: Looks like 3 tenants are affected (tenant-42, tenant-97, tenant-103). Need an urgent rotation + RBAC hardening plan.

tj: which tenants exactly? any PII exposed or just the tokens? short-lived creds?

elaine: tenant-42, tenant-97, tenant-103. No obvious PII in the payloads we saw, just the bearer tokens (they're long-lived service tokens created by the partner integration). Created ~2025-11-03 according to metadata. I ran a quick grep on the partner logs bucket:

```
# sample search
gsutil ls gs://partner-logs-prod/** | xargs -n1 gsutil cat | grep -E "tenant-(42|97|103)" -n
# found entries with header: Authorization: Bearer sk_live_*** (masked here)
```

ram: Proposed immediate plan (6-hour window):
1) Revoke the partner-webhook service tokens for the 3 tenants (invalidate at our vault and partner side)
2) Rewrap KMS aliases used to encrypt partner secrets (rotate alias -> new-key -> re-encrypt)
3) Rotate Vault transit key for partner integration and re-wrap existing secrets
4) Short-term mitigation: issue tenant-scoped, short-lived tokens (TTL 1h) for partner while we finish rollout
5) RBAC: tighten Vault policies so partner role cannot export raw creds to external logs (deny write of token field to partner-facing paths)

jun: I can run audit queries to map any accesses from the partner IP ranges and list which services used those tokens. Will search Cloud Audit Logs / BigQuery for read/write to secret paths. Example query I'll run: 
```
SELECT protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, resource.labels.project_id, timestamp
FROM `project.audit_logs.audit_log_*`
WHERE protoPayload.request.metadata."x-tenant-id" IN ('tenant-42','tenant-97','tenant-103')
  AND protoPayload.methodName LIKE '%access%'
  AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
```

kate: Can we canary this? I'd prefer rotate tenant-103 first (lowest traffic) and validate partner acceptance before full blast.

elaine: Agreed. Assignment: tj -> revoke tokens + notify partner contact; ram -> KMS rewrap + alias rotation; jun -> audit log evidence + list of impacted services; kate -> run canary rotate tenant-103 and validate partner handshake; I'll coordinate comms and update runbook. Target: initial revocation + canary within 2 hours, full rotation within 6 hours.

tj: ack. I'll revoke at Vault (transit revoke + cred delete) and send partner temporary creds. Commands I'll run: 
```
# revoke in Vault
vault kv metadata delete secret/partners/tenant-42/partner-webhook || true
vault write auth/token/revoke-by-id <token-id>
# partner API call
curl -X POST https://partner.example.com/api/revoke -d '{"token":"<token>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $MY_NOTIFY_TOKEN'
```

ram: For KMS rewrap I'll create new cryptoKey versions and re-encrypt blobs. Steps:
- create new key version: gcloud kms keys versions create --key=partner-wrap-key --location=global --keyring=redwood
- re-encrypt S3/GCS blobs via a small job that pulls, decrypts with old key, encrypts with new key and uploads to secure bucket
I'll also rotate KMS alias to point to new primary after verifying rewrap success.

jun: I'll also output a short CSV of principalEmails that used these tokens and post it in the thread when done. If we see any IAM impersonation, we escalate to oncall.

deploy-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/partner-token-rotation (scheduled window pending) :calendar:

elaine: RBAC change note for infra: we need a policy freeze for partner role so it cannot create tokens with unlimited TTL. Proposed policy snippet to enforce TTL <= 1h for partner roles: 
```
# Vault policy pseudo
path "auth/token/create" {
  capabilities = ["create"]
  policy = "if creating_role == 'partner-webhook' then ttl <= \"1h\" end"
}
```
We can implement via sentinel or Vault plugin if needed. Also add audit log filters to alert if tokens are written to external logs.

kate: Canary plan for tenant-103:
- revoke old token (tj)
- issue new short-lived token and rotate KMS alias (ram)
- notify partner with new creds and have them post a test webhook to /health
- run smoke checks on tenant-103 flows (search, sync)
I'll post results here after the test.

ram: One caveat — partner uses an onboarding script that hardcodes the KMS alias name for decryption. We'll coordinate with them to accept the new alias or use alias versioning. Might require a small partner-side deploy window.

elaine: Communication plan: I'll send partner-oriented email template and escalate to partner engineering lead. After rotation, we will request deletion of any archived logs on their side and provide the rotation proof-of-work (audit IDs). Also file a JIRA for post-incident policy changes and a follow-up retrospective.

jun: Found 12 distinct principals that used the tokens; 2 unusual IPs flagged (added to the spreadsheet). Posting CSV in 10m.


tj: tenant-42 revoked. Partner confirmed receipt for tenant-42. Moving to tenant-103 canary once ram finishes rewrap.

kate: canary completed for tenant-103: partner sent test webhook, all checks green. No service regressions.

ram: KMS rewrap done for tenant-103 and tenant-42. Will start tenant-97 next.

elaine: Good work team. After tenant-97 completes, we'll close this thread and open a short postmortem doc (include timeline, root cause: partner onboarding script logging full headers to artifact store, remediation: RBAC + audit rule + partner contract change).


deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: SEC-2026-321 (priority P2) — runbook checklist attached.

elaine: Final ask before we close: ops please run a scrub job to find any other S3 buckets with partner logs older than 180 days and flag for deletion. Also rotate any remaining long-lived partner tokens to TTL 1h. Thanks everyone. :lock:
